free_tier.stated: No fixed quota. Own fair-use policy: 'We place no absolute limit within the 2-month period on the total volume of user data that may exist in a data upload area at any one time' and 'we ... expect that volumes would not exceed 10 Terabytes under normal circumstances.'
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: Retention: transit area purged after 2 months if not submitted; once submitted, ENA is permanent

egress.terms: Unmetered and anonymous. ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk is CORS-open (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) and already served through Cloudflare (`Server: cloudflare`), so CF is in front by default.

tooling: Webin-CLI (github.com/enasequence/webin-cli), plus plain FTP/Aspera. Read side is plain HTTPS/FTP with HTTP range support — works with rclone's http/`sftp` remotes and curl.
chaining: One Webin account = unlimited studies. The upload area is a transit buffer (10 TB documented expectation), while *published* accessions are permanent and unmetered on the read side. Multiply across accounts/centres; read side needs no account at all, so the fetch workload is uncapped regardless of how many deposit accounts exist.

limits.value: Retention: transit area purged after 2 months

limits_note: per-object-cap: none documented per file; per-request volume soft-capped at ~10 TB per 2-month window per upload area, and upload areas are not backed up. Retention: transit area purged after 2 months if not submitted; once submitted, ENA is permanent. Binding constraint on READ is per-ip-shaping: single stream 45 KB/s, 8 parallel ranged GETs 430 KB/s (9.6x).

reliability_note: Upload path is the weak side — FTP sessions drop out, Aspera recommended; upload area is explicitly 'not backed up'.
